text:
Sometimes—but not always. One price comparison found a BLUETTI AC180 kit for **$649**, versus **$748** for the same listed parts bought separately, a **$99 saving**. It also listed an EcoFlow kit at **$669** versus **$848** for its parts, saving **$179** ([price comparisons](https://powersized.com/solar-generator-kits/)).

But discounts can make separate purchases cheaper: another comparison estimated an AC180 plus a third-party 200W panel at about **$659**, below a **$729** bundle ([comparison](https://dealectric.com/solar-generator-kit-vs-buying-separately)).

So compare the bundle with the exact station and panel prices you’d pay separately, and make sure any separate panel’s voltage and connector are compatible.

judge.top_pick: BLUETTI AC180 + 200 W Solar Panel Kit
products: BLUETTI AC180 + 200 W Solar Panel Kit
judge.why: The answer's main figures ($649 vs $748, the $99 saving, and the EcoFlow kit) come from powersized.com. The dealectric.com link is cited only for a secondary counterexample, and the answer names the BLUETTI AC180 kit as its main example without clearly recommending one product.
